newsitem.title: POLAND: Ukraine seeks rapid free trade deal with Poland.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine seeks rapid free trade deal with Poland.

text.p: Ukraine's Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko said in Poland on Tuesday the two countries were working towards an agreement on freer trade which could boost their exchanges by $500 million this year alone.
Lazarenko said after meeting Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski in Warsaw that completion of work on this deal had been the most important theme of their talks.
He said Polish-Ukrainian trade had reached $1.5 billion in 1996, the largest such bilateral exchange in the region.
"If only this (agreement) can be concluded in the first half of this year, then during the current year we can increase trade exchanges by $500 million," he told a news conference.
Kwasniewski and Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma signed a memorandum in January, like one Poland clinched with Russia last year, on their desire to liberalise trade and create a free trade zone.

Lazarenko suggested the deal could be clinched during a visit by Kwasniewski to Kiev in May, when the presidents are also due to sign a declaration of reconciliation between two neighbours whose relations have sometimes been troubled. But Polish officials said much work was still needed on the agreement freeing up trade.

Lazarenko said Ukraine, which is not a member of the World Trade Organisation, had clinched a similar memorandum with Slovakia, was seeking them with Budapest and Prague and hoped to have agreements with seven countries by the year's end.
His two-day trip was devoted largely to economic matters, and touched only briefly on the two countries' increasingly close strategic partnership.
On Monday the two clinched deals aimed at promoting cross-border transport and customs cooperation -- part of a process aimed at freeing traffic across the frontier.
Last year Warsaw and Kiev agreed on visa-free travel for their citizens, which awaits the settlement of final details before Poland's government allows it to take effect.
Lazarenko said the two countries would also approach the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) for funding to further improve border customs posts.

Poland has offered government guarantees for credits to expand production of Polish Bizon combine harvesters in Kovel in Ukraine and the two sides also discussed production of farm machinery in Kharkov, among other initiatives.
Polish leaders thanked Ukraine for not opposing Warsaw's bid to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation.

They also stressed that they wanted a charter to be signed setting out NATO's relations with Ukraine, like one planned between NATO and Russia, and expressed support for Kiev's closer links with various European structures.
